edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: In lege praecepit Dominus coeli terrae marisque: Nolite, inquit, adorare deos inanes, De manibus vestris factos ex ligno vel auro; Indignatio mea nevos disperdat ob ista. Gens ante Mosen rudis, sine lege morata, Nesciensque Deum, morientes deos orabant, Ad quorum effigies faciebant idola vana. Translatis Judaeis Dominus de terra Aegypti, Imposuit legem postmodum, et ista praecepit Omnipotens, sibi soli deservire, non illis. De resurrectione quoque docetur in ipsa, Et spe, fortunatum rursum in aevo vivendi, Idola si vana relinqantur, neque colantur.
pass_a_gloss: In the law the Lord of heaven and earth and sea commanded: Do not, He says, worship empty gods, made by your hands from wood or gold; My indignation will destroy the nations because of these things. The nation before Moses was rude, lived without law, and not knowing God, they were asking dying gods, they were making empty idols to their likenesses. The Lord transferred the Jews from the land of Egypt, afterwards He imposed the law and the Omnipotent commanded these things, to serve Him alone, not those. It is also taught about the resurrection in it, and the hope, to live again in a fortunate age, if empty idols are abandoned and not worshiped.
pass_b_english: The Lord of heaven, earth, and sea commands in the law: "Do not worship empty gods made by your hands from wood or gold; my indignation will destroy the nations because of these things." Before Moses, the nation was crude, living without law and not knowing God; they prayed to dying gods and made empty idols in their likeness. The Lord brought the Jews out of Egypt, then imposed the law, and the Almighty commanded these things: to serve him alone, not them. The law also teaches the resurrection and the hope to live again in a blessed age, if empty idols are abandoned and not worshiped.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The title 'Worship of the One God' captures the thought of the passage.
